stances.claim: The FLP Professorial Chair Series must start high and maintain the standard Dean Candelaria set -- 'he immediately lifted the issue of liberty and prosperity to the international plane.' The Series is not just an academic exercise but the institutional vehicle for propagating the Liberty and Prosperity Under the Rule of Law philosophy in all major law schools.
stances.rhetorical_move: standard-setting-by-inaugural-choice: Dean Candelaria's lecture quality as the benchmark that all future chair holders must meet or exceed
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing institutional expectation

stances.claim: The APJR's discontinuation by CJP's successors -- causing the World Bank to delete it from its website -- is the single greatest institutional failure of the post-Panganiban Court. CJP's expressed hope that CJ Sereno (with her Ateneo economics degree and UP law degree) will continue and update Davide's program is both a compliment and a call to action.
stances.rhetorical_move: institutional-continuity call: the APJR deletion as the cautionary tale; Sereno's qualifications as the basis for hope
stances.confidence: asserted as a diplomatic institutional suggestion

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered September 19, 2012 as the closing remarks at the inaugural lecture of the FLP Chief Justice Panganiban Professorial Chair Series -- the first lecture delivered by Dean Sedfrey M. Candelaria at Ateneo de Manila Professional Schools -- this brief address by CJP opens with the sharpest honorarium presentation in the corpus: 'The Bible says man does not live by bread alone. And I add, neither can he live without it. So here is the check for one hundred thousand pesos for your professorial chair.' He notes that Dean Candelaria 'set a very high standard' and 'immediately lifted the issue of liberty and prosperity to the international plane.' He reflects on his lifelong Ateneo aspiration ('too poor; had to peddle newspapers and shine shoes; both parents died in college'), noting he finally got to speak at the 2006 Ateneo graduation where he predicted a bar topnotcher -- Joan de Venecia became number 1 and three Ateneo graduates made the top ten. CJ Hilario Davide Jr. is present; CJP credits him with the APJR ('so successful the World Bank placed it in its website as a model for all developing countries') and notes with regret that 'our successors in the Court did not find it good enough to be continued'; he expresses hope that incumbent CJ Sereno ('holds an economics degree from Ateneo and a law degree from UP') will continue and update it. He briefly restates his judicial philosophy (strict scrutiny for civil liberties; deferential interpretation for economic matters) and describes the Global Forum (October 2006) where CJ Beverley McLachlin suggested adding 'Under the Rule of Law' -- then 'fell in love with the Philippines, especially with Ateneo de Manila, that she stayed four more days; Ateneo gave her a Doctoral Degree in Law, Honoris Causa. So you have a co-alumnus, the Chief Justice of Canada by the name of Beverley McLachlin.'
